messages.text: Hamilton hopes for 'awesome' Verstappen fight for win

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver hopes he can battle Max Verstappen for Bahrain GP in Malaysia win after F1 qualifying front-row | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver hopes he can battle Max Verstappen for Bahrain GP in Malaysia win after F1 qualifying front-row Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton to start on a Grand Prix front row together for the first time since 2023; Drivers expecting challenging conditions with high tyre wear; watch the race at 8am on Sunday with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 13:31, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's wholesome reaction to qualifying on front row at Bahrain GP in Malaysia Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row. ​Hamilton produced "probably my best lap of the year" to claim second on the grid with his last attempt of qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit, his second front-row start of the year. It will be the first time Verstappen and Hamilton, the grid's two-most successful drivers and the sport's biggest names, have started at the head of a Grand Prix together since July 2023, at that year's Hungarian Grand Prix. messages.text: 'Three tenths backwards' - Wolff admits confusion over Mercedes upgrades

metadata.summary: Toto Wolff has admitted his surprise at Mercedes' major upgrade package for the Bahrain Grand Prix having appeared to take the team backwards, following an underwhelming qualifying display.
metadata.content: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admits confusion over lack of qualifying pace following upgrades at Bahrain GP in Malaysia | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admits confusion over lack of qualifying pace following upgrades at Bahrain GP in Malaysia Mercedes endured a disappointing qualifying display in their upgraded car as Kimi Antonelli was fourth and George Russell eighth; Max Verstappen took pole ahead of Lewis Hamilton; watch the race at 8am with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 13:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of qualifying at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit Toto Wolff has admitted his surprise at Mercedes' major upgrade package for the Bahrain Grand Prix having appeared to take the team backwards, following an underwhelming qualifying display. Despite dominating the 2026 season, Mercedes have brought far fewer upgrades than their rivals at the front of the grid, which meant anticipation had built around the addition of their first major package since May. The Silver Arrows arrived in Malaysia, which is hosting the event due to ongoing conflict in the Middle East, off the back of three successive race victories, and most expected that streak to continue with the help of the upgrades. messages.text: Verstappen beats Hamilton to pole in Malaysia

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen beats Lewis Hamilton to pole position to claim first Red Bull pole of 2026 Formula 1 season | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen beats Lewis Hamilton to pole position to claim first Red Bull pole of 2026 Formula 1 season Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together for the first time in over three years; George Russell will be in seventh after poor qualifying; watch the Bahrain GP in Malaysia at 8am with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Sepang Saturday 3 October 2026 12:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of qualifying at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Verstappen and Hamilton will share the front row in Sunday's race at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, for the first time since Hungary 2023 after the Red Bull driver delivered a dominant qualifying performance. The Dutchman topped each segment of qualifying and set two laps good enough for pole, ending up 0.298s faster than Hamilton who will target a second Ferrari win of the season. messages.text: Antonelli fastest from Verstappen ahead of qualifying in Malaysia

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Max Verstappen ahead of qualifying at Sepang International Circuit | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Max Verstappen ahead of qualifying at Sepang International Circuit Championship leader Kimi Antonelli topped final practice in Malaysia from Max Verstappen; watch Qualifying later on Saturday at 9am with the race itself on Sunday at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Sepang Saturday 3 October 2026 07:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A mystery object brings out the red flag and stops final practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position. Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, struggled on Friday but was 0.278s quicker than Verstappen. Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar took third ahead of Russell fourth but both drivers were more than half a second behind Antonelli, who appears to have found a nice rhythm in time for qualifying later on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 , at the Sepang International Circuit. metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Scandinavia seeks sixth Group 1 in Prix du Cadran | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Scandinavia seeks sixth Group 1 in Prix du Cadran Arc weekend gets under way at ParisLongchamp on Saturday with Gold Cup hero Scandinavia looking well-placed to land the Prix du Cadran; Ascot plays host to domestic action with Thunder Call and Mezcala in the feature contest Thursday 1 October 2026 18:30, UK Image: Scandinavia headlines the Prix du Cadran Scandinavia takes on Queenstown and Caballo De Mar as Arc weekend gets underway - live on Sky Sports Racing . 4.00 ParisLongchamp - Star stayer Scandinavia bids for a sixth Group 1 success Superstar stayer Scandinavia is the headline act on Day 1 of the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe meeting. Aidan O'Brien's prolific winner heads a field of 10 for this Prix du Cadran . He arrives unbeaten in his past eight starts recording a staggering five Group 1 wins in the process and looks hard to oppose as he heads up in distance once again. Stablemate Queenstown , the ride of Wayne Lordan, heads the likely dangers. He returned with an excellent victory in Group 3 company at the Curragh in August before chasing home Scandinavia in the Irish St Leger. messages.text: Erdogan ends Elliott’s title hopes with second-round submission

metadata.summary: Paul Elliott was one victory away from the biggest moment of his career, but Shamil Erdogan ensured it never arrived at ONE Fight Night 48.
metadata.content: Shamil Erdogan ends Paul Elliott's title hopes with second-round submission at ONE Fight Night 48 | MMA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Shamil Erdogan ends Paul Elliott's title hopes with second-round submission at ONE Fight Night 48 Paul Elliott suffered a second-round submission defeat to Shamil Erdogan in the early hours of Saturday morning at ONE Fight Night 48; a victory could have given Elliott the chance to contend for the vacant ONE Heavyweight MMA World Championship Saturday 3 October 2026 11:40, UK Image: Paul Elliott (left) was beaten via submission by Shamil Erdogan in the early hours of Saturday morning (Credit: ONE Championship) Paul Elliott was one victory away from the biggest moment of his career, but Shamil Erdogan ensured it never arrived at ONE Fight Night 48. Undefeated Turkish fighter Shamil Erdogan submitted the Brit in the headliner at Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium in the early hours of Saturday morning, extending his perfect record to 14-0 and bringing Elliott's title ambitions to an abrupt halt. For Middlesbrough-born heavyweight Elliott, the bout represented a golden opportunity to secure a shot at the vacant ONE Heavyweight MMA World Championship and claim the biggest victory of his career against the toughest opponent he had faced to date.
